Docket 1.3.119

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *A server that turns away Meta AI's search crawler is now caught.* Docket asks your server for your homepage as
  each AI search crawler, to find a firewall or CDN refusing one your robots.txt allows. Meta-WebIndexer was not
  asked, so a server refusing it looked clean. It is now asked, using the identifier Meta publishes. As with the
  others, when a CDN that checks crawlers by their network address challenges Docket's request, Docket says it
  cannot verify that from your machine, rather than calling it a block.
- *A logo repeated on every page no longer makes a page a layout-shift risk.* A site's logo, without a declared
  size, in its header and again in its footer, made a page with one properly sized picture read as two unsized
  images out of three, and Docket called it at high risk of layout shift. Measured in a browser, nothing on it moved.
  A page is now called high risk only when one of its own images has no size. A page whose own picture is unsized
  is still reported.
- *A theme's site-name heading is no longer taken for the page's headline.* Some themes put the site's name in a
  main heading on every page, above the page's own. A contact page titled "Contact", with "Contact" as its own
  heading, was reported as promising one thing in search and another on the page, because Docket compared the title
  with the site name. A heading the whole site repeats is now read as the site's, and the page's own heading is the
  one compared.
- *A comment avatar is no longer taken for your logo.* On a blog whose header names the site in text, the first
  picture linking to the homepage was the author's avatar beside a reply in the comments, and Docket reported the
  logo's alt text as missing on every post the author had replied on. Links a page marks as not vouched for, as
  blogs mark comment links, and avatar images are no longer read as the logo. A logo of the site's own with no
  alt text is still reported.

99 checks across 13 areas.
